The EU’s List of Acquisitions website was updated today with details of a deal struck in June between Apple and Samplab, a Swiss startup that described itself as offering “music production for the age of AI.” Here are the details.

Apple’s string of AI deals continues

Last week, the List of Acquisitions section of the EU’s DMA website was updated with details on Apple’s move to acqui-hire Huxe, a startup founded by former NotebookLM engineers that specialized in generating personalized audio briefings and podcast-style content using AI.

Today, the list was updated yet again, revealing another deal involving Apple and an AI audio company.

Apple Inc. (“Apple”), through a subsidiary, will acquire certain assets of Samplab GmbH (“Samplab”) and offer employment to and hire certain Samplab employees. Samplab develops audio editing tools. Apple (together with its group companies) designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services.

Following the deal, Samplab’s website now redirects to Apple’s, while its social media accounts and YouTube channel appear to have been scrubbed of their previous posts and videos.

Previously, Samplab’s website described its “ultimate audio editor for musicians” as a tool that allowed creators to “edit audio files as if you were working with MIDI.” It also touted its ability to:

Detect and edit chords


They stay in key when you change them.
You can even export them as a midi file.

Make any samples sound good together


Samplab matches their tempo and key.
Easily adapt chords, melodies and drums.

Granular stem separation


Separate stems in any audio and
freely modify individual notes.

While Apple has not commented on the acquisition, it isn’t hard to imagine Samplab’s technology eventually making its way into Logic Pro or GarageBand, or even enhancing the audio editing capabilities of Final Cut Pro.

What do you think Apple will do with Samplab’s technology? Let us know in the comments.
